phase3.rule.057.text: Subphase 3A is considered closed when Phase 3 is clearly defined as a governed materialization layer; when the document's mother law is installed as a single central principle; when `Output Block`, `Report Package`, the minimum audience policy, and the realistic MVP scope are fixed without ambiguity; and when the phase appears as a compact architecture capable of producing strong documentation without exceeding the system's support.

phase3.rule.058.text: Define the transversal thematic architecture of the `Report Package` as the grammar that allows multiple fronts of the case to be organized without turning that organization into free invention. Its function is to distinguish material block type from transversal thematic layer, fix the MVP's minimum layers, and establish how themes and subthemes emerge from traceable upstream objects in order to produce a deep, integrated, and disciplined reading.

phase3.rule.059.text: Without transversal thematic architecture, the report falls into one of two forms of poverty. Either it becomes a succession of correct but disconnected blocks, unable to produce systemic vision. Or it compensates for that weakness with prestigious sections, decorative subtitles, and false sophistication.

phase3.rule.060.text: This subphase matters because thematic architecture does not only discipline what may be shown. It also enables genuine documentary power: the capacity to articulate multiple fronts of the case, reveal cross-dependencies, order non-trivial tensions, and make intelligible the structure of constraints, trade-offs, and validation paths that define the case as a system.

phase3.rule.061.text: That Phase 3 defines the thematic architecture means that it may decide which fronts of the case deserve visibility, how to group them, which themes require greater development, and in what sequence they should be exposed. That authority is documentary and structural. It does not consist of freely deciding what would be interesting to say, but of organizing already supported content in a readable way.

phase3.rule.062.text: Its authority consists in organizing, articulating, and making visible already supported content without exceeding the epistemic status of the case. Thematic architecture exists to make the report more powerful, not more arbitrary.

phase3.rule.063.text: Phase 3 architecture operates across two distinct dimensions.

phase3.rule.064.text: The first is the **material block type**. This includes forms such as:

phase3.rule.074.text: The material type defines the visible function of the block, its form of compaction, and the kind of documentary operation it can perform.

phase3.rule.075.text: The second is the **transversal thematic layer**. Each block may belong to one or more layers such as:

phase3.rule.081.text: The thematic layer does not define what kind of block the block is, but from which front of the case it is being read. This double structure allows depth without unnecessarily inflating material ontology.

phase3.rule.082.text: The **`technical_layer`** makes visible technical structure, operating tensions, plausible mechanisms, material constraints, and functional dependencies of the case.

phase3.rule.083.text: The **`regulatory_layer`** makes visible plausible regulatory pressure, preliminary regime, applicable flags, timing windows, and validation dependency needed to confirm applicability.

phase3.rule.084.text: The **`financial_layer`** makes visible preliminary economic logic, CAPEX/OPEX constraints, viability sensitivity, tariff exposure, preliminary compatibility with financial mechanisms, and relevant benefits when support exists.

phase3.rule.085.text: The **`prioritization_layer`** makes visible preliminary order of attention, reasons for focus, relative urgency, blockages, sequences, and action constraints.

phase3.rule.086.text: The **`validation_lineage_layer`** makes visible how the current state of the case is supported, what strengthens or weakens it, what depends on benchmark, prior, hypothesis, or field experience, and why the next validation matters.

phase3.rule.087.text: These five layers do not exhaust case reality, but they stabilize a sufficient transversal grammar so that the document may grow without losing structure.

phase3.rule.088.text: Themes and subthemes do not emerge only from the block type, nor only from the audience, nor from the LLM's free prose. They emerge from the combination of active upstream objects, materially admissible blocks, activated thematic layers, and real relevance for understanding, prioritization, or validation.

phase3.rule.089.text: A **theme** is understood as a material reading front of the case. A **subtheme** is understood as a material refinement of that front when the reading requires more granularity in order to remain faithful and useful. **Structured technical narrative** is understood as the legitimate operation that articulates blocks, themes, and dependencies so that the reader can understand why a front matters, what conditions it, and how it connects to other fronts of the case.

phase3.rule.090.text: That technical narrative is admissible when it orders already supported relationships. It ceases to be admissible when it fills gaps, invents causality, or uses fluent reading to simulate closure.

phase3.rule.091.text: Phase 3 may produce broad, detailed, technically absorbing, financially serious, regulatorily useful documents that are pleasant to read because of their organization. That depth is not a secondary luxury. It is part of the Reporting Engine's reason to exist.

phase3.rule.092.text: Documentary depth must increase articulation, traceability, and systemic intelligibility, not epistemic force. A document may become richer because it better separates fronts, makes cross-dependencies visible, better organizes tensions, and makes a complex system readable. It does not therefore become more conclusive.

phase3.rule.093.text: Phase 3 may use base documents, methodological frameworks, and admitted references to enrich structure, framing, thematic taxonomy, and order of exposition. That use is legitimate when it makes the document more mature and better organized.

phase3.rule.094.text: Those materials do not replace local evidence, do not harden claims by themselves, and do not activate substantive themes that the case does not materially support. Their value lies in disciplining documentary construction, not in lending epistemic authority to the case.

phase3.rule.095.text: Within the MVP, the `Report Package` may legitimately aspire to look like a **technical-operational-financial-regulatory internal evaluation bounded to the case**. That formulation should be read as a valid ambition of documentary robustness, not as a promise of terminal closure.

phase3.rule.096.text: The report may feel serious, deep, and structurally mature. It may give the impression of reading the case from the inside. But that impression must come from articulated density and not from overassertion.

phase3.rule.097.text: Thematic decoration is blocked. Themes, subthemes, or sections whose main function is to sound sophisticated, fill space, or imitate consulting style without real material load must not enter.

phase3.rule.098.text: If a front does not improve understanding, prioritization, validation, or traceability, it should not enter. Structural elegance is desirable; empty ornamentation is not.

phase3.rule.099.text: Confusing thematic architecture with license to invent content.

phase3.rule.100.text: Treating documentary depth as a synonym for greater truth.

phase3.rule.101.text: Using audience alone to determine which themes exist.

phase3.rule.102.text: Replacing structured linkage with articulate but non-traceable prose.

phase3.rule.104.text: Multiplying themes through sector prestige or superficial density.

phase3.rule.105.text: Phase 3 does define the thematic architecture of the report.

phase3.rule.106.text: That architecture exists both to discipline and to strengthen the document.

phase3.rule.107.text: Theme, subtheme, and structured technical narrative are distinguished as different operations.

phase3.rule.108.text: Material block type and transversal thematic layer are distinct and complementary dimensions.

phase3.rule.109.text: The MVP's minimum layers are fixed as `technical_layer`, `regulatory_layer`, `financial_layer`, `prioritization_layer`, and `validation_lineage_layer`.

phase3.rule.110.text: Documentary depth may grow through articulation and organization, not through increased epistemic force.

phase3.rule.111.text: Base documents may enrich structure and framing, but not replace case support.

phase3.rule.112.text: The internal evaluation policy is authorized in a bounded sense.

phase3.rule.113.text: Any thematic decoration without material function is blocked.

phase3.rule.114.text: Subphase 3A.3 is considered closed when thematic architecture is defined as a positive capability of the Reporting Engine and not only as a defensive mechanism; when material type, thematic layer, theme, subtheme, and structured technical narrative are differentiated without conceptual noise; and when the document may aspire to an integrated reading of the case without departing from the mother law fixed in 3A.

phase3.rule.115.text: Define the sectoral theme library as the Reporting Engine's capacity to expand coverage, depth, and industrial differentiation without sliding into narrative arbitrariness or content fabrication. Its function is to fix the multi-level architecture of sector modules, themes, and subthemes and the disciplined rules under which they are activated.

phase3.rule.116.text: An overly short thematic scheme impoverishes the report, makes the case generic, and loses real second-order tensions. An overly loose scheme turns depth into documentary theater. This subphase matters because it enables serious breadth and at the same time prevents empty exuberance.

phase3.rule.117.text: Sectoral richness is not a secondary concession of the system. It is a central capability of the Reporting Engine. Without it, the report could not capture real operating constraints, infrastructure dependencies, regulatory frictions, prioritization structures, or sectoral conflicts that a generic scheme cannot express with enough value.

phase3.rule.118.text: Allowing sectoral breadth and depth means authorizing the `Report Package` not to remain limited to a short catalog of general themes. It may open industry modules, specialized themes, second-order subthemes, and extensive documentary developments whenever the case warrants it.

phase3.rule.119.text: Documentary breadth may grow aggressively when the case demands it, as long as activation remains traceable, materially pertinent, and useful for understanding, prioritization, or validation. Sectoral expansion should not be read as a deviation from the framework, but as a condition for the document to have real technical value.

phase3.rule.120.text: The thematic architecture of the `Report Package` operates at four levels:

phase3.rule.125.text: This hierarchy is conceptual and normative. Its job is to order depth, not to produce premature technical implementation.

phase3.rule.132.text: These layers stabilize document reading across industries and allow sectoral depth to grow over a common skeleton.

phase3.rule.133.text: Over those layers, sectoral modules may be activated such as:

phase3.rule.143.text: The list is not exhaustive. A module enters when case structure makes it pertinent, not because the sector is prestigious or because the document would “look better” with more labels.

phase3.rule.144.text: Within each module, main themes may be activated such as:

phase3.rule.192.text: `conflict between operational uptime and retrofit windows`

phase3.rule.193.text: These lists are illustrative. Their function is to show expected breadth, not to fix a closed catalog.

phase3.rule.194.text: Thematic activation cannot depend on editorial taste or LLM improvisation. It must respond to the combination of industry or asset family, active upstream objects, detected tensions, conflicts, candidate opportunities, plausible regulatory exposure, visible financial constraints, operational criticality, evidence gaps, validation agenda, and real value for understanding or prioritization.

phase3.rule.195.text: A theme or subtheme should enter only if it improves material understanding of the case, preserves relevant conflict, alters prioritization, strengthens the validation agenda, or clarifies operating, regulatory, or economic constraints. If it does not perform any of those functions, its activation is decorative and must be blocked.

phase3.rule.196.text: Thematic architecture operates on `Output Blocks`; it does not replace them. The same material type may participate in very different thematic fronts, and the same theme may require blocks of several types.

phase3.rule.197.text: This double structure allows variety without chaos. It gives depth without inflating block ontology and enables rich documents without giving up material discipline.

phase3.rule.198.text: Phase 3 may aspire to produce extensive documents, with multiple sections and subsections, several fronts open at the same time, and strong technical, regulatory, financial, and operational density. That depth is part of the system's expected capability.

phase3.rule.199.text: Sectoral depth is not an ornamental expansion of the system, but a condition for the report to capture second-order tensions, real operating constraints, infrastructure dependencies, regulatory frictions, and prioritization structures, and not merely descriptive richness.

phase3.rule.200.text: The breadth of the document may grow; the epistemic force of the case may not. Thematic richness should increase systemic reading, not claim strength.

phase3.rule.201.text: Phase 3 may use technical literature, sectoral references, and admitted methodological frameworks to enrich taxonomy, order of exposition, and documentary framing. That use is legitimate when it makes the report more refined and better structured.

phase3.rule.202.text: It is not legitimate to use them to make what remains benchmark look local, to harden claims, or to fabricate subthemes that the case does not materially activate.

phase3.rule.203.text: `Manufacturing / process industry`: may activate `steam systems`, `steam trap reliability`, `condensate return constraints`, `distribution losses`, `insulation condition`, `compressed air`, `leak persistence`, `pressure optimization`, `compressor staging`, `process heat`, `thermal integration opportunities`, `heat recovery conflicts`, `production-critical thermal loads`, `power quality`, `voltage events`, `harmonic exposure`, `losses due to poor power quality`, `low-capex fast-payback measures`, `operational shutdown constraints`, and `sequencing of interventions`.

phase3.rule.204.text: `Buildings / smart buildings`: may activate `HVAC controls`, `scheduling logic`, `setpoint discipline`, `economizer behavior`, `reheat conflicts`, `envelope and thermal demand`, `occupancy mismatch`, `retrofit constraints`, `tariff and peak exposure`, `peak demand penalties`, `control opportunities`, `comfort vs efficiency tension`, `maintenance maturity`, `BMS visibility gaps`, `preliminary regulatory pressure`, and `readiness for retro-commissioning`.

phase3.rule.205.text: `Oil & Gas / industrial utility environment`: may activate `hazardous-area constraints`, `instrumentation reliability`, `steam and thermal losses`, `uptime-critical systems`, `compliance pressure`, `maintenance access constraints`, `electrification conflicts`, `flare / vent / loss-related process considerations`, `asset integrity interaction`, and `decision timing under operational risk`.

phase3.rule.206.text: `District energy / thermal networks`: may activate `network topology relevance`, `generation mix`, `thermal storage logic`, `demand mismatch`, `solar integration feasibility`, `waste heat integration`, `hydraulic configuration constraints`, `expansion path dependence`, `capex intensity vs solar fraction`, and `economic sensitivity under tariff scenarios`.

phase3.rule.207.text: Within the MVP, the `Report Package` may legitimately aspire to look like a **deep, sector-informed technical-operational-financial-regulatory internal evaluation bounded to the case**.

phase3.rule.208.text: It should feel serious, deep, and useful. It must also remain epistemically honest. Its value lies in organizing multiple tensions of the case into a powerful reading, not in imitating a terminal closure the phase does not possess.

phase3.rule.209.text: Any thematic activation whose value is mainly ornamental is blocked: empty subthemes, prestigious branches with no function, long lists that do not change the reading, beautiful but useless taxonomies, and sectoral density used as an aesthetics of expertise.

phase3.rule.210.text: Confusing thematic breadth with increased truth.

phase3.rule.211.text: Activating subthemes only because they are typical of the sector.

phase3.rule.212.text: Using sectoral depth to cover uncertainty or evidence weakness.

phase3.rule.213.text: Treating documentary expansion as suspicious by default and impoverishing the report.

phase3.rule.214.text: Confusing sector references with case-specific support.

phase3.rule.215.text: Sectoral richness is authorized as a central capability of the Reporting Engine.

phase3.rule.216.text: Multi-level thematic architecture is formally fixed.

phase3.rule.217.text: Sector modules are expandable and non-exhaustive.

phase3.rule.218.text: Themes and subthemes activate only through material pertinence, traceability, and real usefulness.

phase3.rule.219.text: Documentary breadth may grow aggressively when the case requires it.

phase3.rule.220.text: Sectoral depth increases documentary value, not epistemic force.

phase3.rule.221.text: Base documents may enrich sectoral structure, but not replace support.

phase3.rule.223.text: Subphase 3A.4 is considered closed when the sectoral theme library is defined as a broad, deep, and disciplined capability; when the system may grow documentarily without arbitrariness; and when thematic expansion appears no longer as a defensive concession, but as a positive condition for producing reports with true industrial texture.

phase3.rule.224.text: Define the minimum pipeline through which Phase 3 transforms structured upstream objects into visible, verifiable, and registrable `Output Blocks`. Its function is to close the nature of the input, the MVP's minimum transformation sequence, the pipeline's control unit, the separation between selection, mapping, construction, verification, and registration, and the formal intermediate output on which later assembly will rest.

phase3.rule.225.text: Without a pipeline, the step from upstream records to visible text would tend to happen through narrative continuity rather than controlled transformation. That weakens traceability, erases the material function of each piece, and obscures the relation between support and exposure.

phase3.rule.226.text: The pipeline does not exist only to prevent overstatement. It also exists to ensure that each visible block reaches assembly with a clear function, legible support, coherent thematic placement, and real potential to contribute to a strong systemic reading of the case.

phase3.rule.227.text: The input of Phase 3 is not free text. Phase 3 consumes exclusively:

phase3.rule.231.text: the already closed block taxonomy and thematic architecture

phase3.rule.232.text: and, when appropriate, admitted base documents only as structural or contextual support

phase3.rule.233.text: Free notes, unregistered intuitions, uncontrolled narrative drafts, and any non-traceable input remain outside.

phase3.rule.234.text: The MVP's minimum pipeline contains six stages:

phase3.rule.235.text: **Governed intake.** Receives the universe of candidate objects relevant to the case.

phase3.rule.236.text: **Selection of admissible material.** Decides which objects deserve to enter rendering based on material relevance and real function.

phase3.rule.237.text: **Thematic-material mapping.** Assigns each selected object to a block type, thematic layer, possible audience, and documentary function.

phase3.rule.238.text: **Disciplined block construction.** Generates the visible block using only the material authorized by its type and purpose.

phase3.rule.239.text: **Block verification.** Reviews linkage, limits, verbal proportionality, audience compatibility, and material function.

phase3.rule.240.text: **Registration for assembly.** Incorporates approved blocks into the `output_block_register`.

phase3.rule.241.text: The sequence is not bureaucratic. It is the minimum infrastructure required for each block to reach assembly with clear identity, recognizable support, and real documentary usefulness.

phase3.rule.242.text: The pattern `upstream object -> final report` is prohibited. The formal pipeline rule is `upstream object -> governed block -> assembly`.

phase3.rule.243.text: Among others, flows must be blocked where `hypothesis_register` feeds a final summary directly, `opportunity_candidate_matrix` becomes a visible recommendation, `validation_queue` is transformed without mediation into a roadmap, or an artifact circulates without caption and without semantic control.

phase3.rule.244.text: The pipeline's control unit is the `Output Block`. The pipeline does not operate on full chapters or finished packages. It operates on minimum units capable of carrying function, limits, traceability, and assembly potential.

phase3.rule.245.text: A section is too large for fine control. The block allows precise selection, localized degradation, punctual blocking, and disciplined reassignment.

phase3.rule.246.text: Selection does not imply automatic inclusion. A valid upstream object does not thereby gain the right to appear in the report.

phase3.rule.247.text: It should only advance if it changes the reading of the case, preserves a relevant tension, affects prioritization, explains a blockage, strengthens validation, or prevents overreading. Exhaustiveness alone is not sufficient.

phase3.rule.248.text: Mapping must happen before any compaction. First lineage, block type, thematic layer, possible audience, limits, and documentary function are fixed. Only then is the visible block summarized or formulated.

phase3.rule.249.text: Summarizing before classification usually produces distortion: conflicts that sound minor, hypotheses that look like conclusions, or validation agendas that already sound like action plans.

phase3.rule.250.text: The pipeline must allow semantic force to be degraded, material to be moved toward `uncertainty_block` or `conflict_block`, reassigned into the validation agenda, or completely blocked from visible circulation.

phase3.rule.251.text: These outcomes do not indicate system failure. They indicate that the architecture retains control when the case does not support strong exposure in the form first considered.

phase3.rule.252.text: Base documents may intervene only to enrich thematic mapping, structural framing, or block organization. They may not close hypotheses, replace local support, or harden claims.

phase3.rule.253.text: The formal output of 3B.1 is the **`output_block_register`**.

phase3.rule.254.text: It contains blocks that are already selected, mapped, constructed, verified, and ready for assembly or audit. It is the first fully governed material output of Phase 3.

phase3.rule.255.text: Treating the Phase 3 input as a prior narrative of the case.

phase3.rule.256.text: Converting upstream records directly into final text.

phase3.rule.257.text: Selecting by exhaustiveness instead of by function.

phase3.rule.258.text: Compacting before fixing lineage and function.

phase3.rule.259.text: Using sections as the pipeline control unit.

phase3.rule.260.text: Preventing degradation or blocking and forcing exposure by inertia.

phase3.rule.261.text: The input of Phase 3 is structured and traceable.

phase3.rule.262.text: The MVP's minimum pipeline contains exactly six stages.

phase3.rule.263.text: The pipeline control unit is the `Output Block`.

phase3.rule.264.text: No upstream object may jump directly to the final report.

phase3.rule.265.text: Selection is not equivalent to mandatory inclusion.

phase3.rule.267.text: The pipeline must allow degradation, reassignment, and blocking.

phase3.rule.268.text: The formal output of the subphase is the `output_block_register`.

phase3.rule.269.text: Subphase 3B.1 is considered closed when the path from upstream objects to governed blocks is unequivocal, sufficient, and does not require silent reinterpretation in order to produce visible material of high documentary quality.

phase3.rule.270.text: Define the assembly of the `Report Package` as a governed composition operation built from already admitted blocks, projected into specific views and complemented by subordinated artifacts. Its function is to close what the package exactly is, how it is composed, what relationship it has to the MVP's views, which minimum composition rules it must obey, how sparse cases must be treated, and what the formal output of this stage is.

phase3.rule.271.text: Without this subphase, assembly would tend to behave like free drafting of the final document. Views would become parallel writing engines, artifacts would become persuasive channels, and the package would lose its fine link to the blocks that support it.

phase3.rule.272.text: This subphase matters because the `Report Package` must not only compose admissible blocks. It must also be capable of making the case intelligible as a system, where sequence, contrast between fronts, thematic articulation, and artifact subordination contribute to systemic understanding rather than to the mere accumulation of correct pieces.

phase3.rule.273.text: The `Report Package` is not a monolithic document or a sovereign narrative piece. It is a governed composition of previously admitted blocks, ordered to produce an integrated reading of the case.

phase3.rule.274.text: Its value lies in the organized whole. It may contrast fronts, show dependencies, group materials that reveal trade-offs, and build progressions that move from technical structure toward validation and prioritization implications. That compositional sophistication is legitimate when it remains subordinate to the case's real support.

phase3.rule.275.text: The `Report Package` may be composed only from the **`output_block_register`**. Any direct assembly from upstream records, loose text, free notes, or ad hoc formulations generated during composition is blocked.

phase3.rule.276.text: The reason is structural: if the package could incorporate content outside the block register, assembly would effectively become a second analytical instance.

phase3.rule.277.text: `technical_view` and `executive_view` do not create content. They are disciplined projections of the available universe of blocks.

phase3.rule.278.text: They may select, reorganize, compact, or exclude admitted blocks, but they may not introduce new semantics. Their job is to modulate access and reading density without producing another version of the case.

phase3.rule.279.text: For the MVP, `technical_view` is the structurally more complete base view. `executive_view` derives from it through controlled compaction.

phase3.rule.280.text: This hierarchy matters because the executive view should simplify access, not govern the case first and let the technical one qualify it afterward. Executive reading may not sound more conclusive, erase material conflict, or hide critical uncertainty.

phase3.rule.281.text: Artifacts are subordinated to the `Report Package`. They may circulate only if they improve material understanding of the case and if their reading can remain faithful to the support of the blocks that sustain them.

phase3.rule.282.text: Every visible artifact must be accompanied by an `artifact_caption_block` or equivalent semantic control. The artifact does not replace the block nor create a parallel truth channel; it amplifies understanding when it remains within the same limits as the rest of the package.

phase3.rule.283.text: Assembly must obey at least these rules:

phase3.rule.284.text: **Minimum coverage.** The package must cover, when the case requires it, technical state, relevant uncertainty, material conflicts, validation agenda, and preliminary priority or next-step logic.

phase3.rule.285.text: **No theatricality.** Pieces are not added merely so that the package “looks complete.”

phase3.rule.286.text: **No empty duplication.** The same content should not be repeated unless its function or audience changes.

phase3.rule.287.text: **Balance.** There may not be overexposure of opportunity with underexposure of uncertainty or conflict if the case remains open.

phase3.rule.288.text: **Semantic hierarchy.** Order must serve understanding, not persuasion.

phase3.rule.289.text: In addition, composition may use contrast between fronts, sequences showing dependency, and groupings that reveal trade-offs when this improves systemic reading.

phase3.rule.290.text: A valid `Report Package` may be short, asymmetrical, dominated by uncertainty, with little or no visible opportunity, with a validation agenda taking precedence, and with no artifacts.

phase3.rule.291.text: The package's validity does not depend on symmetry or on an appearance of completeness. A sparse case must be allowed to circulate as a brief, honest, and useful reading, even when its main value is to clarify uncertainty and orient validation.

phase3.rule.292.text: An admitted block does not necessarily enter both views. The law of compressibility is fixed as follows: **if a block cannot be compacted without losing critical limits, it should not enter `executive_view`**.

phase3.rule.293.text: Exclusion by view is not a loss of coverage. It is a legitimate decision of fidelity.

phase3.rule.294.text: Although this subphase does not design UI or final layout, there must still be a minimum reading logic. The sequence of the package should favor case orientation, technical structure, conflict and uncertainty, candidate opportunity where applicable, validation agenda, and next steps.

phase3.rule.295.text: Packages that open with proposed action or a persuasive artifact before orienting the reading are blocked.

phase3.rule.296.text: The formal output of 3B.2 is the **`view_assembly_manifest`**.

phase3.rule.297.text: This manifest determines which blocks enter which view, in what order, with what degree of compression, with which associated artifacts, and under what circulation restrictions.

phase3.rule.298.text: Treating the package as monolithic text drafted from scratch.

phase3.rule.299.text: Assembling it from sources outside the `output_block_register`.

phase3.rule.300.text: Using views as parallel writing engines.

phase3.rule.301.text: Designing the executive view first and attaching the technical one afterward.

phase3.rule.302.text: Treating artifacts as visual persuasion rather than subordinated comprehension aids.

phase3.rule.303.text: Forcing symmetry and density in sparse cases.

phase3.rule.304.text: The `Report Package` is a governed and integrative composition.

phase3.rule.305.text: Its exclusive assembly source is the `output_block_register`.

phase3.rule.306.text: `technical_view` is the base view and `executive_view` derives from it.

phase3.rule.307.text: Artifacts are subordinated and not autonomous.

phase3.rule.308.text: Composition may be sophisticated when it improves systemic understanding.

phase3.rule.310.text: View compressibility governs inclusion or exclusion.

phase3.rule.311.text: The formal output of the subphase is the `view_assembly_manifest`.

phase3.rule.312.text: Subphase 3B.2 is considered closed when `Report Package` assembly is defined as a disciplined, integrative, and non-sovereign operation; when the relationship among blocks, views, and artifacts is unequivocal; and when composition can produce a holistic reading of the case without breaking the mother law of Phase 3.

phase3.rule.313.text: Define how the mother law of Phase 3 governs rendering. Its function is to fix three principles: every visible output inherits limits in addition to content; no rendering operation may harden the case; and if a format loses visible support or detaches critical restrictions, semantics must degrade.

phase3.rule.314.text: An output may be well written, well ordered, and visually clear, and still betray the case if conflict, uncertainty, assumptions, or validation dependency were lost during rendering. This subphase matters because Phase 3's main risk is not only inventing content, but silently hardening real content through format change.

phase3.rule.315.text: Every interpretive surface of the package inherits limits in addition to content. The rule covers blocks, views, artifacts, captions, titles, headers, labels, tables, order of exposition, and any other signal that guides reading.

phase3.rule.316.text: Inheritance includes both what the material allows to be said and what it prevents from being said. A faithful output preserves the epistemic contour that defines the real force of what it materializes.

phase3.rule.317.text: No rendering operation may increase the epistemic force of the material it processes. This applies to writing, summary, titling, ordering, visualization, compaction, view reassignment, and assembly.

phase3.rule.318.text: A hypothesis does not become confirmation because it is better written. A conflict does not become reconciliation because it is compacted. A candidate opportunity does not become a decision because it changes position or view.

phase3.rule.319.text: Compacting does not mean softening. Any valid compaction must preserve conditionality, material conflict, critical uncertainty, validation dependency, and any limit without which the block would change meaning.

phase3.rule.320.text: If a block cannot be compacted while preserving those critical limits, that compaction is not admissible.

phase3.rule.321.text: Inheritance operates by material dependency rather than by textual proximity. A block inherits limits from all upstream objects necessary to sustain it, not only from the last object mentioned or from the nearest fragment.

phase3.rule.322.text: This matters especially in composite blocks, summaries, opportunities, and views that condense several blocks. Documentary fragmentation cannot be used to drop inconvenient limits.

phase3.rule.323.text: `technical_view` and `executive_view` inherit the same epistemic contour even though they do not expose the same volume of text. The executive view may reduce density, but it may not reduce the case's substantive restrictions.

phase3.rule.324.text: Less text does not mean fewer limits.

phase3.rule.325.text: Artifacts and captions are subject to the same general rule. If they cannot make visible, or at least not contradict, conflict, uncertainty, and validation dependency, they should not circulate.

phase3.rule.326.text: Omission is valid only if it does not alter the substantive interpretation of the case. Likewise, reordering may not be used to induce more closure than support allows.

phase3.rule.327.text: Titles, headers, labels, and captions are not an exception; they form part of the interpretive surfaces already covered by the general rule. Many overstatements are born there rather than in the body.

phase3.rule.328.text: If, during rendering or assembly, a block loses visible support, changes view, is strongly compacted, or becomes detached from part of its restrictions, it may become mandatory to degrade its semantic intensity.

phase3.rule.329.text: Degradation is not an optional stylistic refinement. It is a duty of fidelity when the new format no longer supports the prior formulation.

phase3.rule.330.text: Epistemic inheritance is not a good editorial practice. It is a circulation criterion. If it fails, the output should not publish, should not export, or must be rewritten and degraded before circulation.

phase3.rule.331.text: Assuming that correct rendering equals epistemic fidelity.

phase3.rule.333.text: Using compaction, order, or reading signals to harden the case.

phase3.rule.334.text: Treating the executive view as if it could expose fewer substantive restrictions.

phase3.rule.335.text: Treating degradation as optional when visible support decreases.

phase3.rule.336.text: Every interpretive surface of Phase 3 inherits limits in addition to content.

phase3.rule.337.text: No rendering operation may harden the case.

phase3.rule.338.text: Compaction requires preservation of critical limits.

phase3.rule.340.text: Views inherit the same epistemic contour even if they differ in density.

phase3.rule.341.text: Artifacts, captions, titles, and labels are subject to the same discipline.

phase3.rule.342.text: Semantic degradation becomes mandatory when format loses support.

phase3.rule.343.text: A failure of inheritance is a cause of non-circulation.

phase3.rule.344.text: Subphase 3B.3 is considered closed when epistemic inheritance is expressed in a central, compact, and sufficient way; when it governs every interpretive surface of the package; and when mandatory degradation is established as a normal response to loss of support.

phase3.rule.345.text: Define the formal output contract of the Phase 3 MVP. Its job is to fix which outputs actually exist, what the minimum function of each one is, what structural relation they hold to one another, and what remains outside the current scope.

phase3.rule.346.text: Without an output contract, Phase 3 ends in a vague notion of “report.” With a contract, it ends in a small, sufficient, and epistemically honest set of governed outputs.

phase3.rule.353.text: This set is sufficient. Any additional output at this stage would be premature proliferation unless a future need is explicitly justified.

phase3.rule.354.text: `report_package`: main documentary output for human consumption.

phase3.rule.355.text: `output_block_register`: formal, auditable register of already governed blocks.

phase3.rule.358.text: `machine_export_bundle`: minimum technical output for traceability, interoperability, and structured handoff.

phase3.rule.359.text: `report_package`: at least one valid view, traceable blocks, disciplined sequence, and preserved inherited limits.

phase3.rule.360.text: `output_block_register`: selected, mapped, constructed, verified blocks ready for assembly or audit.

phase3.rule.361.text: `audience_view_register`: view-specific included blocks, reading order, compression level, circulation restrictions, and allowed artifacts where applicable.

phase3.rule.362.text: `artifact_register`: only artifacts supported by admitted blocks and accompanied by caption or equivalent semantic control.

phase3.rule.363.text: `machine_export_bundle`: enough structure to reconstruct the relation among package, views, blocks, and artifacts.

phase3.rule.367.text: `report_package` composes eligible views, blocks, and artifacts.

phase3.rule.370.text: The following remain outside the MVP as autonomous outputs:

phase3.rule.379.text: If any such content appears, it must live inside the `report_package`, not as an independent product.

phase3.rule.380.text: No MVP output promises final diagnosis, final compliance, final ROI, savings verification, terminal recommendation, or closed empirical verification. `executive_view` does not promise a “nice summary of everything,” `artifact_register` does not promise complete visual coverage, and `machine_export_bundle` does not promise immediate universal integration.

phase3.rule.381.text: A sparse case may legitimately produce a short `report_package`, a minimal `executive_view`, an empty `artifact_register`, and strong validation weight. This does not constitute system failure.

phase3.rule.382.text: Treating “report” as a single totalizing output.

phase3.rule.383.text: Creating new outputs for every marginal documentary need.

phase3.rule.385.text: Treating `artifact_register` as an autonomous truth channel.

phase3.rule.386.text: Requiring symmetry across cases and outputs.

phase3.rule.387.text: The MVP authorizes exactly five formal outputs.

phase3.rule.388.text: Each output has a defined minimum function and structural dependency.

phase3.rule.389.text: The output contract is small, sufficient, and honest.

phase3.rule.390.text: Regulatory, financial, verification, or presentation-driven autonomous outputs remain outside the MVP.

phase3.rule.391.text: Sparse cases are valid configurations of the contract.

phase3.rule.392.text: Subphase 3C is considered closed when the end of Phase 3 ceases to be a vague idea of “report” and is fixed as a brief, precise, and sufficient contract of governed outputs.

phase3.rule.393.text: Define how Phase 3 adapts the same material base to two different audiences without altering conflict, uncertainty, relevant assumptions, validation dependency, or proportional semantic force. Its function is to close what formal difference exists between `technical_view` and `executive_view`, what may be compacted and what may not, when material must be excluded from the executive view, and what language and tone limits govern each view.

phase3.rule.394.text: Without audience policy, the pursuit of clarity would tend to buy readability at the price of epistemic loss. This subphase matters because Phase 3 must not produce two truths, but two distinct accesses to the same case.

phase3.rule.395.text: Well-executed compaction does not impoverish the case; it makes it more readable without breaking its substantive complexity.

phase3.rule.399.text: Separate views for regulatory, financial, investor, operations, or external-audit audiences do not yet exist. Those fronts appear inside the two permitted views as thematic layers.

phase3.rule.400.text: The legitimate difference between views may only occur in exposure density, visible volume, trace granularity, dependency explicitness, and tolerance for technical detail.

phase3.rule.401.text: They may not differ in case epistemic status, material conflict, critical uncertainty, validation dependency, semantic direction of visible claims, or substantive interpretation.

phase3.rule.402.text: `technical_view` is the base view of maximum explicitness allowed in the MVP. Its function is to expose with greater density case structure, tensions, constraints, dependencies among blocks, and validation agenda.

phase3.rule.403.text: Greater explicitness does not mean greater truth. It means less compression.

phase3.rule.404.text: `executive_view` exists to reduce reading friction, condense active fronts, improve documentary rhythm, and lower cognitive load.

phase3.rule.405.text: It does not exist to soften the case, hide hard limits, or turn the package into persuasion. It may and should make the document more elegant and accessible, provided that it does not change the substantive interpretation.

phase3.rule.406.text: To compact means to reduce visible volume without reducing substantive restrictions. Any valid compaction must preserve conditionality, material conflict, critical uncertainty, validation dependency, relevant blockages, and the block's real function.

phase3.rule.407.text: If a block cannot be compacted while preserving its critical limits, that compaction is not admissible.

phase3.rule.408.text: Valid compaction improves orientation, rhythm, and readability. It does not rewrite the case.

phase3.rule.409.text: Not all blocks are equally compressible.

phase3.rule.413.text: `next_steps_block` when the steps are already bounded

phase3.rule.417.text: certain simple tables of stabilized evidence

phase3.rule.422.text: complex tables whose summary would induce overreading

phase3.rule.423.text: If a block cannot be compacted without damage, it must remain only in `technical_view`, be semantically degraded, or leave `executive_view`.

phase3.rule.424.text: No block has an automatic right to be present in the executive view.

phase3.rule.425.text: The executive view may not use terminal language if the base block does not support it. The technical view may not inflate certainty through density or technicality. Both views must prefer conditional grammar when the case requires it.

phase3.rule.426.text: Titles, headers, subtitles, labels, and captions are also subject to these rules.

phase3.rule.433.text: are blocked whenever support remains preliminary, conflictive, conditional, or validation-dependent.

phase3.rule.434.text: Legitimate adaptation reduces friction, improves order, compacts repetition, and makes access to the case more elegant while preserving substantive complexity without losing readability. Deformation hardens language, erases limits, hides conflict, or presents maturity the case does not have.

phase3.rule.435.text: The rule is explicit: **clarity is admissible; simplification that alters interpretation is not**.

phase3.rule.436.text: **Example 1 — Correct compaction from technical to executive summary**

phase3.rule.441.text: `Correct:` “Electrification remains conditioned by conflict among candidate opportunity, unvalidated electrical capacity, and site operating constraints.”

phase3.rule.443.text: A `conflict_block` that depends on uptime restriction, uncertainty about electrical capacity, and retrofit window should not enter `executive_view` if compaction removes any of those conditions.

phase3.rule.446.text: `Correct:` “Primary validation focus under current analytical structure”

phase3.rule.449.text: `Correct:` “Confirm drive applicability, operating profile stability, and control feasibility before elevating variable-speed intervention beyond candidate status.”

phase3.rule.450.text: Treating `executive_view` as the simpler and therefore more conclusive version of the case.

phase3.rule.451.text: Using clarity to justify erasing conflict or uncertainty.

phase3.rule.452.text: Designing the executive view to persuade and the technical view to qualify later.

phase3.rule.453.text: Keeping in `executive_view` blocks whose compaction removes critical limits.

phase3.rule.454.text: Confusing adaptation to the reader with the right to soften the case.

phase3.rule.456.text: The difference between views is one of density and compaction, not truth.

phase3.rule.457.text: `technical_view` is the base view of maximum explicitness.

phase3.rule.458.text: `executive_view` exists to improve access and readability without altering interpretation.

phase3.rule.459.text: Compressibility is differential by block type.

phase3.rule.460.text: Exclusion by incompressibility is a legitimate fidelity decision.

phase3.rule.461.text: Clarity is admissible; simplification that alters reading is not.

phase3.rule.462.text: Subphase 3D is considered closed when audience policy stops sounding like a defensive restriction and instead operates as a discipline of readability: able to reduce friction and improve the document without degrading the case's substantive complexity.

phase3.rule.463.text: Fix the final circulation barrier of Phase 3 through a brief and sufficient central law capable of deciding whether a visible output may circulate without proliferating micro-controls.

phase3.rule.464.text: Phase 3 does not need a publication bureaucracy. It needs a clear final barrier against misleading circulation.

phase3.rule.465.text: The mother law fixed in 3A operates here as the final barrier: **no visible output of Phase 3 may say more than what is supported by the upstream objects on which it depends**.

phase3.rule.466.text: Exactly three consequences follow from that law:

phase3.rule.467.text: **Do not invent content.** Nothing may circulate if it cannot be mapped to traceable upstream objects or to admitted structural framing.

phase3.rule.468.text: **Do not hide material limits.** Nothing may circulate if it erases or dilutes conflict, uncertainty, critical assumptions, or validation dependency that remain material.

phase3.rule.469.text: **Do not harden through presentation.** Nothing may circulate if summary, order, compaction, visualization, caption, or view induces a reading stronger than the case actually supports.

phase3.rule.470.text: When an output cannot circulate as-is, Phase 3 may only produce:

phase3.rule.476.text: `publish` means the output may circulate as-is.

phase3.rule.477.text: `degrade` means it may circulate only with lower semantic force.

phase3.rule.478.text: `reassign` means it must not circulate in that view or form and must be relocated.

phase3.rule.479.text: `hold_for_validation` means it must not circulate as a visible finding, but must remain alive in the validation agenda.

phase3.rule.481.text: A sparse case is not a system failure. It may produce a short, asymmetrical output dominated by uncertainty or validation, and it should be allowed to circulate that way if it honestly represents the case.

phase3.rule.482.text: Artificial completeness, filler sections, empty artifacts, and generic summaries used to conceal structural weakness are blocked.

phase3.rule.483.text: Honest publication makes the case visible with exactly the force it supports, even if that produces an uncomfortable, brief, or fragile output.

phase3.rule.484.text: Misleading publication is any output that appears to have more closure, more maturity, or more decisional clarity than support really allows, whether through omission, compaction, order, artifact, title, or tone.

phase3.rule.486.text: `Incorrect:` “The best measure is to electrify the thermal system.”

phase3.rule.487.text: `Correct after degrade:` “Electrification remains a candidate pathway conditioned on validation of electrical capacity, operating compatibility, and real load sequence.”

phase3.rule.489.text: Case: a technically valid block cannot enter `executive_view` without losing critical limits.

phase3.rule.490.text: `Correct:` reassign it to `technical_view` and leave in the executive view only a brief formulation that preserves the real blockage.

phase3.rule.492.text: Case: there is a hypothesis with analytical value, but it still does not support exposure as a visible finding.

phase3.rule.493.text: `Correct:` move it into the validation agenda or a critical dependency instead of presenting it as a mature insight.

phase3.rule.495.text: `Correct:` short package, uncertainty dominant, validation agenda visible, little candidate opportunity, and no artifacts.

phase3.rule.496.text: `Incorrect:` fill it with generic summary, empty subtitles, or irrelevant tables so that it “looks complete.”

phase3.rule.497.text: Turning final control into a long list of minor gates without a central criterion.

phase3.rule.498.text: Allowing circulation of non-traceable content by “general sense.”

phase3.rule.499.text: Using omission or order to produce a more mature reading of the case.

phase3.rule.500.text: Treating the sparse case as a defect to be fixed with filler.

phase3.rule.501.text: Keeping ambiguous states instead of deciding among the authorized outcomes.

phase3.rule.502.text: Visible circulation in Phase 3 is governed by a single mother rule.

phase3.rule.503.text: Exactly three operational consequences derive from that rule.

phase3.rule.504.text: Upon failure, only five outcomes are permitted.

phase3.rule.505.text: The sparse case is a legitimate configuration.

phase3.rule.506.text: The distinction between honest publication and misleading publication is fixed as the final circulation barrier.

phase3.rule.507.text: Subphase 3E is considered closed when final circulation control has been reduced to an unequivocal law, a minimum set of consequences, unambiguous outcomes, and a clear distinction between honest publication and misleading publication.

phase3.rule.508.text: Define the completion criterion of Phase 3 and the exact point from which its design can be handed to implementation without silent reinterpretation. Its function is to fix what is frozen, what may vary technically without breaking the phase, what the MVP's minimum integrity proof is, why that proof must include a sparse case, and what remains explicitly outside the current closure.

phase3.rule.509.text: Phase 3 is not closed by written volume or by aspiration to completeness. It closes when its documentary logic no longer depends on implementation finishing the job of deciding what the phase means.

phase3.rule.510.text: Closure by sufficiency is not system poverty. It is a condition of serious implementability. It guarantees that the technical layer will be able to build the Reporting Engine without reopening its epistemic scope, its material grammar, or its output contract.

phase3.rule.511.text: When Phase 3 closes, implementation may not reinterpret:

phase3.rule.513.text: the prohibition against turning Phase 3 into an inference, verification, final compliance, or terminal recommendation engine

phase3.rule.518.text: and the three already consolidated central semantic laws:

phase3.rule.522.text: These decisions are non-negotiable for implementation.

phase3.rule.532.text: degree of automation of renderers, exporters, validators, or assemblers

phase3.rule.533.text: and the MVP's effective visual richness

phase3.rule.534.text: None of those variations may reopen the conceptual contract, alter epistemic inheritance, erase visible limits, create unauthorized views, or substitute structure with free improvisation.

phase3.rule.535.text: Phase 3 may only be declared closed if it can sustain, at least conceptually, an end-to-end path that includes:

phase3.rule.545.text: and application of the visible circulation rule

phase3.rule.546.text: This proof does not yet require full implementation. It requires sufficient structural coherence so that implementation no longer has to reinterpret the phase in order to make it exist.

phase3.rule.547.text: In addition to a relatively rich case, the phase must support a minimum proof with a sparse case where:

phase3.rule.550.text: the validation agenda weighs more than opportunity

phase3.rule.552.text: and the output remains publishable without artificial filler

phase3.rule.553.text: This second proof is not optional. It protects the MVP against false completeness.

phase3.rule.554.text: Phase 3 closes by MVP sufficiency, not by exhausting possibilities. It does not require maximum industry coverage, an exhaustive subtheme library, a broad visual library, extra stakeholder views, perfect final formats, or advanced customization.

phase3.rule.555.text: It requires only enough for the Reporting Engine to have closed logic, to materialize a case seriously, and not to depend on later reinterpretation in order to exist. That closure by sufficiency does not reduce ambition; it makes ambition implementable as product discipline.

phase3.rule.556.text: The following remains explicitly outside the MVP, even if desirable later:

phase3.rule.565.text: client- or industry-level customization as a finished product

phase3.rule.566.text: These expansions belong to future backlog and do not condition the constitutive closure of Phase 3.

phase3.rule.568.text: `Correct:` implement export first in `Markdown` or simple `HTML`, and later in `PDF`, without changing the conceptual contract of the `Report Package`.

phase3.rule.569.text: `Incorrect:` introduce a new `investor_view` in implementation because “it would be useful,” without prior documentary authorization.

phase3.rule.570.text: **Example 2 — Minimum proof with a relatively rich case**

phase3.rule.571.text: `Correct:` case with multiple blocks, visible conflict, candidate opportunity, validation agenda, `technical_view`, `executive_view`, one or two subordinated artifacts, and consistent structured export.

phase3.rule.572.text: **Example 3 — Minimum proof with a sparse case**

phase3.rule.573.text: `Correct:` short case, dominant uncertainty, visible validation agenda, almost no `opportunity`, no artifacts, and honest publication.

phase3.rule.574.text: `Incorrect:` complete it with generic summary, empty subtitles, and irrelevant tables to “demonstrate robustness.”

phase3.rule.576.text: `Incorrect:` replace `Output Block` with a “free editable section” because it is more convenient for the renderer.

phase3.rule.577.text: `Incorrect:` let implementation use open prompts to “improve” the package's tone without respecting already closed circulation rules.

phase3.rule.578.text: Declaring the phase closed by documentary volume rather than conceptual closure.

phase3.rule.579.text: Letting implementation decide what a block is, what a view is, or what may circulate.

phase3.rule.580.text: Reopening semantic laws for renderer convenience.

phase3.rule.581.text: Accepting minimum proof only with rich cases and not with sparse ones.

phase3.rule.582.text: Requiring sectoral or visual exhaustiveness as a condition for MVP closure.

phase3.rule.583.text: Phase 3 is considered closed when its epistemic, material, and contractual core is frozen for implementation.

phase3.rule.584.text: There is a zone of legitimate technical variation that does not break the phase.

phase3.rule.585.text: The MVP must sustain a minimum end-to-end proof.

phase3.rule.586.text: That proof must exist for both a relatively rich case and a sparse case.

phase3.rule.587.text: Closure by sufficiency constitutes product discipline, not renunciation.

phase3.rule.588.text: Future product expansions remain explicitly outside the MVP.

phase3.rule.589.text: Subphase 3F is considered closed when implementation can already take Phase 3 as a stable documentary contract: sufficiently frozen to be built, sufficiently compact to be governable, and sufficiently powerful to produce serious reports without reopening its meaning in the technical layer.

phase4.rule.001.text: Define the operational constitution of Phase 4 as the layer of the framework that governs the passage from preliminary claims toward explicit routes of evidence hardening. Its function is not to verify by desire or to produce terminal closure, but to take claims, tensions, candidate opportunities, uncertainties, and evidence gaps already structured upstream and convert them into a disciplined architecture in which each relevant claim can be linked to required local evidence, baseline hardening, necessary contrast or observation, measurement when applicable, instrumental and operational dependencies, upgrade conditions, and explicit causes of hold, degrade, or block.

phase4.rule.002.text: Without Phase 4 the framework is exposed to two symmetrical failures. The first is to raise claims on the basis of plausibility, benchmark, or pressure for closure without a real hardening architecture. The second is to leave the case trapped in indefinite provisionality, with relevant claims, dominant tensions, and visible candidate opportunities, but without an explicit structure saying what is missing, which evidence actually matters, and under what conditions a claim could legitimately elevate its status.

phase4.rule.003.text: Phase 4 matters because it does not duplicate the general epistemic policing already closed in Phase 0; it makes it operational for the upgrade attempt. Phase 0 fixed the law of claim status. Phase 4 fixes the practical mechanism for trying to harden that status without pretending there is verification where there still is none. Its value is not to make the system timid, but to organize an economy of hardening: to reorder claims by validation value and epistemic cost, to turn tensions, operating frictions, regulatory triggers, and candidate opportunities into explicit architecture of evidence, baseline, and observability, and to prepare the passage toward field verification without false closure.

phase4.rule.004.text: Phase 4 is the Verification Bridge of the framework. It is the layer that takes the already structured upstream universe and decides which claims deserve an explicit hardening route, which local evidence matters for them, which baseline must be hardened, which observation or contrast must occur, which measurement applies when it applies, which dependency of instrumentation, access, or operation conditions the upgrade, and which cause obliges the claim to remain in hold, degrade, block, or do_not_upgrade within a delimited domain of validity.

phase4.rule.005.text: Phase 4 is not a final audit, compliance certification, closed savings verification, or a sovereign measurement stack. Nor does it exist to redo Phase 2 or to extend Phase 3 with verification language. Its work begins exactly where the case has already been structured and made legible, but has not yet been hardened through material routes of local support.

phase4.rule.006.text: The entry rule for Phase 4 is strict: only that which can be treated as a legitimate claim-hardening candidate within an explicit upgrade architecture enters. Not every visible hypothesis enters, nor every candidate opportunity. What enters is that which, due to material relevance, validation value, and capacity to change the reading of the case, deserves to be subjected to a governed hardening route.

phase4.rule.008.text: selection and prioritization of `claim_upgrade_candidate` from claims, tensions, candidate opportunities, uncertainties, and evidence gaps already structured upstream;

phase4.rule.009.text: explicit statement of required local evidence per claim;

phase4.rule.010.text: definition of baseline hardening when the claim depends on a baseline that still does not support upgrade;

phase4.rule.011.text: identification of required contrast, observation, documentary capture, or measurement when appropriate;

phase4.rule.012.text: explicit statement of instrumental, operational, temporal, and access dependencies;

phase4.rule.013.text: fixation of upgrade conditions and of causes for hold, degrade, block, or do_not_upgrade;

phase4.rule.014.text: delimitation of the domain of validity within which the claim could elevate its status.

phase4.rule.015.text: A technical claim derived from a dominant refrigeration tension enters, for example, when Phase 2 has already shown insufficient local evidence and high validation value. In that case, Phase 4 may treat it as a relevant `claim_upgrade_candidate` and link it to required local evidence such as setpoints, cycles, alarms, and operating logs, to baseline hardening need, to an observation or measurement stub, and to an explicit do_not_upgrade rule until the real control architecture is confirmed. The bridge does not state that the claim has already hardened; it makes visible what would need to happen for it to harden.

phase4.rule.016.text: A regulatory claim also enters when Phases 1 and 2 suggest plausible regulatory pressure but a real field trigger is still missing. In that case Phase 4 does not state that it “applies.” It converts that reading into required local evidence, an upgrade condition, a field-specific dependency, and an explicit block against elevation until the trigger is confirmed.

phase4.rule.017.text: The following remain outside the MVP:

phase4.rule.018.text: final compliance and any form of terminal regulatory certification;

phase4.rule.021.text: exhaustive sensor, meter, or instrumentation design;

phase4.rule.025.text: full verification modeling or simulation at product-final scale;

phase4.rule.027.text: Also outside the MVP is treating every visible hypothesis as if it deserved a bridge. A generic lighting opportunity, with low material relevance, high uncertainty, and low impact on the reading of the case, does not necessarily need to enter Phase 4. It may stay outside hardening prioritization, remain as a low-priority backlog item, or receive no bridge yet. The Verification Bridge does not exist to dignify every intuition with the same methodological weight.

phase4.rule.028.text: The central unit of Phase 4 is the **`claim_upgrade_candidate`**. That unit governs the phase because it preserves continuity with the claim-centered architecture, keeps explicit the guiding question of Phase 4 — whether a claim may or may not attempt to elevate its status — and forces hardening to be treated as a governed operation on the claim rather than as a scattered collection of technical tasks.

phase4.rule.029.text: `claim_upgrade_candidate` is the correct unit because it:

phase4.rule.030.text: preserves continuity with the framework, where the claim is the governing unit;

phase4.rule.031.text: avoids making measurement sovereign too early;

phase4.rule.032.text: supports different hardening routes without collapsing the phase into a single technique;

phase4.rule.033.text: allows the change in claim status to be governed explicitly;

phase4.rule.034.text: and allows promising claims and claims that must remain in hold, degrade, block, or do_not_upgrade to be treated under the same discipline.

phase4.rule.035.text: This is decisive because Phase 4 does not work over “measurements in the abstract” or over “loose evidence.” It works over delimited attempts at claim upgrade. Measurement may be one route; baseline hardening may be another; documentary confirmation of control architecture may be another; validation of a regulatory field trigger may be another. The center is not the chosen technique. The center is the claim attempting to harden under explicit conditions.

phase4.rule.036.text: Units centered on measurement are too narrow: they make sovereign a route that in many cases is neither the first nor the most pertinent. Units centered on required evidence are too small: they capture missing pieces, but do not by themselves govern the change in claim status. Units centered on verification packages or workstreams are too large and too late: they mix several claims, lose granularity, and make it opaque which exact claim is trying to harden and under what domain of validity.

phase4.rule.037.text: `claim_upgrade_candidate` avoids those drifts. It keeps the focus on the correct question: which concrete claim deserves a hardening architecture, what support it lacks, and under what conditions it could or could not attempt an upgrade.

phase4.rule.038.text: The mother law of Phase 4 is fixed as follows:

phase4.rule.039.text: **No claim may elevate its status in Phase 4 through narrative convenience, need for closure, benchmark, proxy, documentary presentation, or sector plausibility; it may only attempt upgrade if there is an explicit, traceable, and materially pertinent hardening route that increases its support within a delimited domain of validity.**

phase4.rule.040.text: This law does three things at once. First, it prohibits elevation through rhetoric or closure pressure. Second, it requires every upgrade attempt to be tied to a concrete hardening route rather than to a desire for verification. Third, it makes clear that even a successful upgrade remains valid only within a delimited domain and not as license for unrestricted extrapolation.

phase4.rule.041.text: A single anti-example is enough to fix the point: treating benchmark as if it were local validation, calling a non-delimited intuition a `measurement requirement`, or saying that a claim “can now rise” without a baseline, without a target variable, and without required local evidence constitutes bad design for Phase 4. There is no bridge there; there is an unguided epistemic jump.

phase4.rule.042.text: The relationship to Phase 2 is one of strict continuity, not replacement. Phase 2 has already produced the structured universe of inferences, hypotheses, tensions, conflicts, candidate opportunities, uncertainties, evidence gaps, validation queue, and next best questions. Phase 4 does not rediagnose that universe or reason it from scratch again. It takes it as the base from which to decide which claims deserve an explicit hardening route and which do not.

phase4.rule.043.text: This means that Phase 4 does not duplicate the Decision Core. Phase 2 answered what is structurally alive in the case and where tension, uncertainty, and opportunity concentrate. Phase 4 answers which of those fronts justify methodological investment in hardening, which local support actually matters, and which condition blocks or enables an upgrade attempt.

phase4.rule.044.text: The refrigeration case shows this clearly. If Phase 2 detects a dominant refrigeration tension, with insufficient local evidence and high validation value, Phase 4 may elevate that front into a relevant `claim_upgrade_candidate`. From there, the hardening architecture may require setpoints, cycles, alarms, operating logs, baseline hardening, and confirmation of control architecture before any upgrade attempt. Phase 2 identified the tension. Phase 4 designs the explicit route for hardening the claim without pretending the tension has already been verified.

phase4.rule.045.text: The opposite case is equally constitutive. If Phase 2 leaves visible a generic lighting opportunity with low material relevance, high uncertainty, and low impact on the overall reading, Phase 4 is not obliged to dignify it as a bridge candidate. It may leave it outside hardening prioritization or keep it as a low-priority backlog item. The Verification Bridge does not exist to treat everything visible as equally hardenable.

phase4.rule.046.text: The relationship to Phase 3 is equally strict. Phase 3 materialized admissible upstream content into governed visible outputs, but without closing verification, without certifying compliance, and without turning candidate opportunity into terminal decision. Phase 4 begins where Phase 3 ends: when the case is already legible, but still lacks explicit hardening routes.

phase4.rule.047.text: Phase 4 does not use `report_package`, `artifact_register`, or `audience_view_register` as substitutes for verification support. Visible representation may help reveal which claims matter most, which tensions dominate, and where the validation agenda carries more weight. But no caption, table, or artifact may by itself elevate the status of a claim. Reporting makes the case visible. The bridge makes visible what is missing to harden it.

phase4.rule.048.text: The regulatory example again fixes the boundary. If Phase 3 showed plausible regulatory pressure, Phase 4 does not inherit that visibility as if applicability were already confirmed. It converts that reading into required local evidence, field trigger, upgrade condition, and explicit block against elevation until specific confirmation exists. Reporting does not verify. The Verification Bridge does not confuse visibility with support.

phase4.rule.049.text: The positive product of Phase 4 is not a prettier assertion or a stronger claim by wording. It is an **explicit hardening architecture**.

phase4.rule.050.text: That architecture makes visible, for each `claim_upgrade_candidate`, which local evidence actually matters, which baseline must be hardened, which observation, contrast, or measurement applies, which instrumental or operational dependency conditions the attempt, which domain of validity limits the upgrade, and which cause obliges the claim to remain in hold, degrade, block, or do_not_upgrade. In industrial terms, that means turning intuitions about refrigeration, steam, compressed air, BMS, power quality, electrification, or regulatory pressure into governed routes of real support rather than into diagnoses by inertia. It also means revealing the real observability economy of the case: where the site already offers sufficient support, where the baseline remains unstable, and where the claim still depends on access, logging, or measurable boundary that the case does not yet have.

phase4.rule.051.text: That is Phase 4's distinctive contribution. It does not impoverish the framework; it makes it stronger wherever hardening is pertinent. It does not exist to produce thin reports or to extinguish analytical ambition. It exists to convert analytical ambition into legitimate routes of support without pretending closure ahead of time.

phase4.rule.052.text: The realistic MVP of Phase 4 must remain compact. It must be sufficient to govern attempts to upgrade relevant claims without collapsing into a total verification infrastructure.

phase4.rule.053.text: That minimum MVP must be able to sustain, at least:

phase4.rule.055.text: explicit statement of required local evidence per claim;

phase4.rule.057.text: minimum observation, contrast, or measurement routes where materially pertinent;

phase4.rule.058.text: explicit statement of instrumental, operational, and access dependencies;

phase4.rule.059.text: upgrade conditions and causes of hold, degrade, block, or do_not_upgrade;

phase4.rule.060.text: and honest treatment of sparse cases.

phase4.rule.061.text: This implies that measurement is not sovereign. Some claims will harden through logs, field triggers, confirmation of control architecture, local documentary evidence, or operating contrast. Others will require bounded measurement. Others should not enter the bridge yet. The MVP does not need a giant ontology of sensors or a full M&V stack in order to be constitutively valid.

phase4.rule.062.text: The sparse case is decisive in proving that the MVP is well designed. If the case has few strong claims, many evidence gaps, little local material, and dominant uncertainty, Phase 4 must still be useful with fewer `claim_upgrade_candidate`, more blocks, more hold, and a shorter but honest hardening architecture. If the bridge only looks robust when the case already arrives almost hardened, then it is not well constituted.

phase4.rule.063.text: The following would be over-engineering in this constitution:

phase4.rule.064.text: building giant ontologies of sensors or instrumentation;

phase4.rule.066.text: collapsing Phase 4 into full-stack measurement design;

phase4.rule.067.text: attempting final compliance or terminal verification reporting inside the MVP;

phase4.rule.068.text: designing field operational deployment at product-final scale;

phase4.rule.069.text: opening national simulation, live monitoring, or verification dashboards;

phase4.rule.070.text: or turning the phase into an exhaustive M&V layer before the minimum bridge has been closed.

phase4.rule.071.text: It would also be over-engineering to turn every visible hypothesis into a `claim_upgrade_candidate` out of methodological anxiety. The MVP must remain compact precisely in order to concentrate hardening where it truly changes the reading of the case.

phase4.rule.072.text: Treating benchmark as if it were local validation.

phase4.rule.073.text: Treating proxy as if it already authorized upgrade.

phase4.rule.074.text: Calling a non-delimited intuition a `measurement requirement`.

phase4.rule.075.text: Allowing a claim to “rise” without baseline, without target variable, and without required local evidence.

phase4.rule.076.text: Making measurement sovereign and impoverishing other hardening routes.

phase4.rule.077.text: Duplicating Phase 0 as a general warning rather than as a practical mechanism.

phase4.rule.079.text: Using `report_package` or artifacts as if they were sufficient support for upgrade.

phase4.rule.080.text: Taking low-materiality hypotheses into the bridge only for completeness or methodological prestige.

phase4.rule.081.text: Designing Phase 4 so that a sparse case can only look “robust” through filler or pseudo-routes.

phase4.rule.082.text: The anti-example of bad design is unequivocal: a system that takes a plausible opportunity, associates it with a sector benchmark, invents a non-delimited “measurement requirement,” and concludes that the claim can now elevate without hardened baseline, without required local evidence, and without a domain of validity. That is not a Verification Bridge. It is a narrative jump with measurement vocabulary.

phase4.rule.083.text: Phase 4 is defined as a Verification Bridge and not as terminal verification.

phase4.rule.084.text: Its function is to govern the passage from preliminary claims toward explicit hardening routes.

phase4.rule.085.text: The correct central unit of Phase 4 is `claim_upgrade_candidate`.

phase4.rule.086.text: Measurement is recognized as one possible hardening route, not as sovereign over the phase.

phase4.rule.087.text: The mother law of Phase 4 prohibits every upgrade through narrative convenience, benchmark, proxy, sector plausibility, or closure pressure.

phase4.rule.088.text: Phase 4 does not redo Phase 2 or extend Phase 3 with verification language.

phase4.rule.089.text: Its relationship to Phase 2 is one of continuity over structured claims; its relationship to Phase 3 is one of continuity over material already made legible but not verified.

phase4.rule.090.text: The positive product of Phase 4 is an explicit hardening architecture and not a stronger claim by formulation.

phase4.rule.091.text: The MVP of Phase 4 must remain compact and may not collapse into full-stack M&V, final compliance, or national verification deployment.

phase4.rule.092.text: The sparse case is a legitimate bridge configuration and not a defective exception.

phase4.rule.093.text: Subphase 4A is considered closed when there is no longer ambiguity about what Phase 4 is, what it is not, what enters the bridge, what remains outside the MVP, why `claim_upgrade_candidate` is its central unit, what its mother law is, how it continues Phase 2 and Phase 3 without duplicating them, what positive product it contributes, and what constitutes bad design.

phase4.rule.094.text: At that point, future implementation can no longer freely reinterpret Phase 4 as audit, reinforced reporting, sovereign measurement stack, or terminal verification. It may only build it as what has been closed here: a compact, traceable, and serious architecture for attempting to harden relevant claims without pretending support that does not yet exist.

phase4.rule.095.text: Define the central operation of the Verification Bridge for the MVP: how the claims that do deserve real hardening cost are selected and how their explicit routes of evidence, baseline, contrast, observation, or measurement are designed. Its function is to convert an already structured upstream universe into a governed set of `claim_upgrade_candidate` and into explicit hardening pathways, without pursuing exhaustiveness, without collapsing into measurement design, and without introducing upgrade through desire for closure.

phase4.rule.096.text: The existence of Phase 4 is not justified by saying that “more data is needed.” It is justified by knowing how to distinguish between what is still visible but immature and what already deserves real methodological investment in hardening. If 4B fails, the bridge becomes decorative in either of two ways: either it pursues everything plausible and dilutes focus, or it limits itself to producing vague lists of missing items without claim, without boundary, and without pathway.

phase4.rule.097.text: 4B matters because this is where the new capability of Phase 4 becomes operational: organizing an economy of hardening. That means selecting which claims truly deserve support cost, which ones should not consume bridge resources, and how to convert vague uncertainty into concrete dependencies of evidence, baseline, observability, and blocking. That capability does not add rhetoric; it adds structure. A system that only asks for “more data” does not have a bridge.
