phase4.rule.622.text: An admissible technical variation would be to begin with simple serialized registers or basic tables for the seven bridge outputs and later migrate to a relational database or graph structure without changing the semantics of candidate, pathway, baseline hardening, instrumentation gap, decision map, or do-not-upgrade. It is also admissible to change internal orchestration order as long as the result still preserves the same objects and structural relationships.

phase4.rule.623.text: This does not break Phase 4 because it changes implementation, not meaning. The bridge still has the same central unit, the same outcomes, the same output contract, and the same no-upgrade discipline. Technology may change; the phase may not.

phase4.rule.624.text: The following would be improper reopening:

phase4.rule.625.text: turning `hold` and `block` into one single `pending` state because of UI convenience or technical simplicity;

phase4.rule.626.text: eliminating `do_not_upgrade_register` under the excuse that “it can be inferred”;

phase4.rule.627.text: merging required evidence, baseline hardening, and instrumentation gap into free-form notes;

phase4.rule.629.text: Each of these changes breaks the phase even if the software works. The problem is not technological, but semantic. If implementation erases hard differences among outcomes, outputs, or upgrade barriers, it stops building the bridge that the phase closed and starts building something else.

phase4.rule.630.text: A relatively rich case may include technical tensions in refrigeration and sequencing, plausible regulatory pressure, reasonable observability in part of the site, and some additional candidate fronts. The correct minimum proof does not consist in producing a pretty demo, but in demonstrating structural integrity:

phase4.rule.632.text: each one receives its own pathway;

phase4.rule.633.text: required evidence is separated by claim;

phase4.rule.634.text: baseline hardening appears only where it truly matters;

phase4.rule.635.text: instrumentation gaps are partial, not uniform;

phase4.rule.637.text: and `do_not_upgrade_register` remains alive for claims that still cannot rise.

phase4.rule.638.text: If the rich case cannot populate those seven outputs coherently without mixing fronts or losing granularity, Phase 4 is not truly closed.

phase4.rule.639.text: A sparse case may have few eligible claims, predominant evidence gaps, no historian, weak baseline, and high operating uncertainty. The correct minimum proof shows exactly that:

phase4.rule.643.text: baseline hardening more important than the immediate possibility of upgrade;

phase4.rule.647.text: This does not represent failure of the system. It represents structural honesty. If the sparse case had to be filled with soft claims, decorative pathways, or pseudo-upgrades in order to pass the proof, then the bridge would not be reliable.

phase4.rule.648.text: Suppose a technical claim about thermal control or performance whose pathway was well defined in the MVP. The bridge has already been able to do several things:

phase4.rule.654.text: and perhaps leave the claim on `hold` or produce a bounded `upgrade` if local support was sufficient.

phase4.rule.655.text: But there is a point beyond which the bridge can no longer advance through better architecture alone. In order to harden that claim further or enter stronger verification, the following are required:

phase4.rule.658.text: submetering or targeted measurement where appropriate;

phase4.rule.661.text: and confirmation of dominant variables under real site conditions.

phase4.rule.662.text: In many cases, site problems will also appear that the MVP can only anticipate, not resolve: poor tag quality, incomplete export, equipment operating in manual, inability to isolate a subsystem during production, uptime constraints, or lack of temporal synchronization across sources. In compressed air this may mean being unable to distinguish useful load from persistent leakage; in steam balance, failing to close returns or condensate sufficiently; in power quality, lacking waveform or event data in the correct window. That example shows the correct frontier. The MVP can design and govern the bridge. It cannot replace the field evidence that the next layer needs in order to truly exist.

phase4.rule.663.text: The following would be over-engineering in 4E:

phase4.rule.664.text: requiring full-stack integration with historian, logging, and field campaigns before the phase can close;

phase4.rule.665.text: designing the next full verification layer from now on;

phase4.rule.666.text: turning the “what comes next” section into a long and non-hierarchical wishlist;

phase4.rule.667.text: requiring terminal compliance, full M&V, or continuous verification as a condition of current closure;

phase4.rule.668.text: or freezing technical implementation details that are not needed in order to protect bridge semantics.

phase4.rule.669.text: 4E must close the MVP with discipline. It must not force it to solve today what can only exist tomorrow with real field data, more observability, and stronger quantitative rigor.

phase4.rule.670.text: Declaring the phase closed because of written volume and not because of conceptual closure and real minimum proof.

phase4.rule.671.text: Requiring full historian integration before 4E can close.

phase4.rule.672.text: Validating the bridge only with rich cases and not with honest sparse cases.

phase4.rule.673.text: Turning “what comes next” into an open wishlist without clear scaling conditions.

phase4.rule.674.text: Letting implementation redefine candidate, pathway, outcomes, or outputs.

phase4.rule.675.text: Closing Phase 4 as if it already included field verification, final compliance, or terminal packages.

phase4.rule.676.text: Each of these errors distorts the handoff. Either it closes too early and leaves semantics open, or it delays closure artificially by requiring capabilities that already belong to the next verification step.

phase4.rule.677.text: Phase 4 becomes closed when the Verification Bridge already exists as a stable, compact, and buildable methodological contract.

phase4.rule.678.text: Closure freezes semantics, not one single technical implementation.

phase4.rule.679.text: The minimum proof of the MVP must include a relatively rich case and a sparse case.

phase4.rule.680.text: Closure is by sufficiency and not by exhaustiveness.

phase4.rule.681.text: The next serious layer of the framework already requires real field data, greater observability, and more robust baselines.

phase4.rule.682.text: That later continuity does not belong to the current MVP, but it does remain explicitly delimited.

phase4.rule.683.text: Implementation may not reopen central units, outcomes, outputs, structural relationships, or the meaning of upgrade.

phase4.rule.684.text: Phase 4 is not considered closed because of documentary volume or future aspiration, but because of buildable methodological integrity.

phase4.rule.685.text: Subphase 4E is considered closed when there is no longer ambiguity about:

phase4.rule.686.text: what remains frozen when closing Phase 4;

phase4.rule.687.text: what may vary technically without breaking it;

phase4.rule.688.text: what the minimum integrity proof of the MVP is;

phase4.rule.689.text: why that proof requires a rich case and a sparse case;

phase4.rule.691.text: and how the framework continues afterward, under harder conditions that already require real field data.

phase4.rule.692.text: At that point, Phase 4 may be handed to implementation without silent reinterpretation. It becomes sufficiently frozen to be built, sufficiently compact to be governed, and sufficiently honest to make clear that the next serious step can no longer be achieved with more architecture alone, but with verification supported by observability and real site evidence.
